title: The pirate queen who commanded tens of thousands

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1807, a widow took command of tens of thousands of pirates.
beats.visual: Red sails fill the frame on a sketched sea; a lone figure at the prow

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: South China coast: Zheng Yi Sao.
beats.visual: Sketch map of the Pearl River Delta and Guangdong coast; name card in English and Chinese

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Her pirate husband died in 1807, and she took over his fleets. But there was a problem.
beats.visual: PD 1804 drawing of a Chinese junk; red flag rises; husband's silhouette fades

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: They did. Estimates run from 40,000 to 70,000 pirates. They beat Qing fleets and fought the Portuguese.
beats.visual: Counter '40,000–70,000?' with a question mark; CC0 painting of Portuguese ships fighting pirates

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: They never did. In 1810 she negotiated her own surrender. Her crews got amnesty.
beats.visual: Handcuffs fall open; sketched office door; scroll stamped 'AMNESTY'

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: She retired, ran a gambling house, and died in 1844.
beats.visual: Dice roll on a table; candle; '1844'

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: One widow, never captured. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Red sail folds; History Sketches corner logo

description: After her pirate husband died in 1807, Zheng Yi Sao (Ching Shih) took command of one of history's largest pirate alliances off south China, then negotiated her own surrender in 1810 and retired free. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #pirates #chinesehistory
